$schema-note: THE ENUMERATION #565 ASKED FOR, as a committed artifact rather than prose.
A label-dependent check is one whose BEHAVIOUR branches on a pull-request
label. Every such check inherits the label-blind sampling rule: a PR is
CREATED by one API call and LABELLED by a separate one, so the `opened` run
is dispatched before the label exists (measured on PR #555: run created
16:10:42Z, `ci:cheap` applied 16:10:43Z). Anything gated on a label is
therefore exercised only on PRs that get pushed to at least twice, unless it
declares how it copes.
This file is NOT documentation. `check-label-dependence.mjs` compares it
against the tree in two directions — but THE TWO ARE NOT THE SAME
STRENGTH, and this note used to say only 'BOTH directions', which reads as
though they were (#602).
REGISTRY -> TREE is EXHAUSTIVE. Every entry here is checked: its file must
exist, must still branch on a label, and must contain the label it names.
This is the direction that decays, because an entry nobody compares still
READS as though it were guarded.
TREE -> REGISTRY IS BEST-EFFORT, AND IT IS THE ONE YOU ARE ABOUT TO RELY
ON. It fails on the undeclared sites it finds and is SILENT on the ones it
does not. Its reach is whatever `scanTree` walks and whatever
`workflowIsLabelDependent` / `scriptIsLabelDependent` match — READ THOSE
THREE FUNCTIONS rather than trusting this sentence, because they are the
bound and they can be widened without this note changing. As they stand
today they are pattern matches over the TOP LEVEL of two directories, so a
label-dependent site in a subdirectory, in a file type not scanned, or
written in an unrecognised shape is NOT caught.
THE KNOWN BLIND SPOTS, MEASURED (#593), and each pinned as an executable
assertion in check-label-dependence.test.mjs so this list cannot go stale:
CLOSED by #593: `types:` in YAML block-sequence style (the ordinary
idiom — only the flow style `types: [labeled]` was seen before); and
`labels` reached by bracket notation, pull_request["labels"].
STILL NOT DETECTED: `gh pr view --json labels`; octokit
`listLabelsOnIssue`; labels arriving in an arbitrary environment
variable; a destructured `const { GITHUB_EVENT_PATH } = process.env`;
files that are not .mjs/.yml and any subdirectory; and A SECOND
label-dependent site inside an ALREADY-DECLARED file.
Those are ACCEPTED, not pending. The first three read the label at runtime
through a subprocess or an API call, which no static reading of a file can
decide. The destructured read is left alone because keying on the bare
identifier made the guard flag ITSELF. And the already-declared-file case
is not closed with a per-entry site COUNT, because a hand-maintained tally
that every edit must remember to update is the trap this repository keeps
removing — it would go stale silently while reading as verified.
SO: adding your entry here IS checked. FAILING to add it may not be. Do
not read a green run as confirmation that you had nothing to declare.
When the population grows, add the entry AND say how the new check avoids
being verified only by accident of review history.

checks.label: ci:cheap
checks.behaviour: Check E refuses a PR labelled `ci:cheap` whose changed paths trip any filter in test.yml. The lane gate exempts `ci:cheap` PRs from the sequential-PR capacity check, so a mislabelled one consumes a signing-runner slot the gate believes is free.
checks.sampling: SELF-DECLARING. On an `opened` payload an absent `ci:cheap` is not authoritative, so the run computes the tripped filters anyway and announces that classification is DEFERRED, naming them. It exits 0 rather than 2 because exit 2 in the PR path reddens every PR at creation; the claim is deferred, not abandoned, and lane-check.yml checks it. An unreadable payload is CANNOT CHECK (exit 2), never a pass.

checks.label: ci:cheap
checks.behaviour: Runs check-path-filters.mjs on the `labeled` event, when the PR's current label set contains `ci:cheap`, so the lane claim is verified with the label demonstrably present instead of depending on whether someone pushed twice.
checks.sampling: THIS CHECK IS ITSELF LABEL-DEPENDENT, and that is the honest reading: the fix for the sampling rule is a check gated on a label. Its gate reads `github.event.pull_request.labels`, the SAME field check-path-filters.mjs parses — not `github.event.label.name`, the single label that triggered the event. Reading the triggering label meant a PR already carrying `ci:cheap` and then given any other label skipped entirely, suppressing a real finding. The identity of those two fields is asserted by check-path-filters.test.mjs.
